schema.title: Response List Users Api V1 Admin Users Get

post.description:
Invite a user of one of the tenant's verified email domains, as ``invited``.

The worker emails them an invitation (P1b-11); they then sign in from their own
browser, and the first sign-in makes them ``active`` (findings A15). An email that
exists in any tenant is refused: Authentik's usernames are emails, and an email maps
to one tenant (findings A8).

delete.description: P1c-07: delete a user of the admin's tenant with their history; audited.

patch.description:
Change role or status. Deactivated users are refused at sign-in and on every
request; reactivating returns them to ``active``, or ``invited`` if they never
signed in.

post.description: P1c-07: queue the invitation email again for a user who has not signed in yet.

put.description:
Default mode, model and reasoning of a new conversation in the workspace, among
the modes and models the operator enabled for the tenant (P1a-03, P1a-09).

post.description:
Tenant discovery (P1b-06): the methods the address's domain allows. Domain-level
only, so it says nothing about whether the address belongs to a user; an unknown
domain gets the links-only answer, like any domain without SSO.

Clear the session cookies and revoke the session server-side (P1a-02, P1b-08): the
access and refresh tokens are listed in ``revoked_sessions`` and revoked at
Authentik, so a copy of either old cookie is refused.

The tenant admin's code for the second factor of a sign-in link (P1b-08), from the
browser that POSTed the link. A wrong code asks again (at most 5 in 5 minutes).

Renew the session before the access token expires (P1b-08). Needs the refresh
cookie; the previous access and refresh tokens are revoked, so only the new ones
work. A refused refresh clears both cookies (the user signs in again).

Start a sign-in through the address's tenant's source. An unknown domain and a
domain without SSO get the same 409: discovery already tells the page which.

get.description: The active notice in full, its summary, and what the user has accepted.

post.description: Accept the active notice version (idempotent: a second acceptance records nothing).

schema.title: Response List Sources Api V1 Content Sources Get

post.description:
An editor proposes a file (upload) or a URL, with the manifest's metadata. The
licence basis is always required; a licence or permission letter may be attached,
downloadable or not (decision 10, Oct 22, 2026: no letter is required for now).

A reviewer approves a proposal, which queues its ingestion. For a possible
replacement the reviewer names the source it replaces, or keeps both.

get.description: The licence or permission letter on file, as a download.

post.description:
P2A-04: a reviewer takes an ingested source out of retrieval, the library and
downloads for every tenant (D1), without deleting it; its RAGFlow documents are
disabled in this call. A pause never satisfies a takedown.

P1c-14: a reviewer restores a crawled page they withdrew; the next crawl of its
site takes it again as a new register row.
P2A-04: a reviewer resumes a paused source; no re-parse.

post.description:
Start a conversation in a workspace with a mode, model and reasoning, all fixed.

Defaults come from the workspace; the mode is checked against the tenant's
``answer_modes``, the model and reasoning by ``choose_for_new_conversation``
(catalogue, ``enabled_models``, external-models entitlement, reasoning switch and
the external spend cap, P1a-09 to P1a-11). At the cap an external model falls back
to the workspace default and the response carries the notice.

get.description: One tenant, for its console page (P1b-12).

post.description:
Create the tenant's admin as ``invited``, provision them in Authentik and queue
their invitation email (P1b-11).

They then sign in from their own browser; the first sign-in makes them ``active``.
An email already used in any tenant is refused: Authentik's usernames are emails,
and an email maps to one tenant (findings A8).

put.description:
Sign-in links on or off (on by default), JIT provisioning from the tenant's SSO
source, and the MFA requirement for tenant admins. Audited with before and after.

delete.description:
Remove the tenant's source from Authentik; its users then sign in with links (if
the policy allows them) until a source is configured again. Audited.

put.description:
Configure the tenant's one SSO source in Authentik and keep its non-secret fields.

The client secret (OIDC kinds) goes to Authentik only. A new source, or a change of
kind, needs it; otherwise omitting it keeps the one Authentik holds. Audited with
the kind, the source slug and a fingerprint of the stored configuration.

get.description:
Month-to-date token usage and cost by model, from ``usage_ledger``, and external
spend against the cap with the 80 and 100 percent notice thresholds (UTC month).
What the tenant's workspace tag pickers offer (P1b-12).
